title: Make Assignments addressable: ?lifecycle opens its review, ?case and ?job land
tests_added: app/_lib/db/devcase-ledger.test.ts (1 case appended: job filter before the limit)
deviations_from_card: (1) Rebased on slot A's shape, per its builder's notes: filterCases/caseStage no longer exist, so ?job= is a LEDGER QUERY parameter - listCaseLedger gains a `job` filter on dev_cases.job_id (app/_lib/db/devcase-ledger.ts, applied before LIMIT), filterCasesUrl emits &job=, GET /api/devcase passes params.get('job'), useDevTabData threads caseFilters.job. These four files (+ casesPage.ts) replace DevCasesTable.filter.ts's filterCases in the card's write set; CaseFilters gains an optional `job`. (2) ?case= resolves to {selectedCaseId} unconditionally - the reader reads GET /api/devcase/[id], so acceptance 5's raiseLimit and the caseMissing notice are unnecessary: a case past the page opens anyway and a foreign/deleted id gets the reader's existing coded DEVCASE_CASE_NOT_FOUND 404 with the way back. (3) Added a third lifecycle notice, lifecycleOutsideWindow: GET /api/devcase/lifecycle answers the newest 50 only, so an id absent from a full 50-row window cannot honestly be called missing. A failed lifecycle load keeps the intent pending instead of resolving to 'missing'. (4) Catalog keys live under devcase.casesTable (jobFilter, jobFilterUnnamed, clearJobFilter, linkGateDecided, linkLifecycleMissing, linkLifecycleOutsideWindow) - appended at the end of that object, which avoided a nested insert into devcase.studio. (5) Docs: dev-case README (new paragraph), plus one sentence each in docs/features/jobs/README.md (JobsLifecycleStrip is mapped there) and docs/architecture/app-structure.md (tabs.ts is mapped there). The compliance README sentence at :573-576 is now true as written, so it was left alone.
notes: Shell interplay: the shell strips ?tab= via nav.replace(buildUrl({tab:null}, search)) from its own snapshot, which can re-write the query with ?lifecycle= still in it after DevTab stripped it; DevTab's strip effect is keyed on the whole query string, so it strips again, and a re-arrival of the same intent is idempotent (same focus/review). Not browser-verified (no dev server per the brief); an e2e for /?tab=assignments&lifecycle=<id> showing the review panel would be the natural follow-up. test:unit: 9867/9868 - the one BROKEN file is app/_lib/python-runner-concurrency.test.ts ('an aborted spawn kills the whole process tree'), which fails identically when run alone and touches none of this card's files (Windows process-tree environment). test:perf: red only on job-ingest.ts 402/400 (known) and app/api/jds/generate/route.ts 3024/3023, which carries none of this card's files (its graph moved with a sibling's uncommitted app/_lib/db/profiles.ts). app/page.tsx: this card adds 13166 bytes (+1 module); while I held the lock to raise the page ceiling, candidate-profile/B had just committed 060ddba4d raising it to 8681 KB measured on the shared checkout that already contained this card's uncommitted files, so the page now measures 1385 modules / 8676.7 KB against 1385 / 8681 and no perf-budget commit was needed from this card - the coordinator should know that r03 candidate-profile/B's recorded 'share' absorbed this one's ~13 KB. tsc clean except the untracked kpi-sim/ tree.
